docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: To keep it simple, Attributes are the basic building blocks of a character. These are broken down into Primary Attributes, Secondary Attributes, and Tertiary Attributes.

docs.title: Primary Attributes
docs.text:
These are your big ones, strength, agility, etc.

Just about every game, with some exceptions, has some in some form or another within reason. These values are generated with dice and they have some impact, directly on indirectly, on pretty much everything else in the game. As you can imagine these are extremely important.

docs.title: Secondary Attributes
docs.text:
These are your medium ones, your health points, mana points, speed, etc.

These are just as important as the primary attributes. The main difference is that instead of being rolled these values are derived based upon a combination of the Primary Attributes and other factors that may affect your character.

docs.title: Tertiary Attributes
docs.text:
These are your small ones, hair colour, weight, sex, gender, etc.

While your tertiary attributes seldom impact gameplay on a strictly mechanical level, they are important in their own way. These attributes can often have interesting consequences. Being taller might allow one to reach higher or farther, whereas being small might allow you to fit in tighter spaces. Some people might have an affinity or aversion for different sexes and genders. Tertiary attributes are more likely to impact roleplay and how a Game Master makes use of these attributes can have surprising impact.

docs.title: Strength (STR)
docs.text: Strength is a measure of a character's physical strength.

docs.title: Dexterity (DEX)
docs.text: Dexterity is a measure of a character's fine motor control and coordination.

docs.title: Agility (AGI)
docs.text: Agility is a measure of a character's flexibility and mobility.

docs.title: Conditioning (CON)
docs.text: Conditioning is a measure of a character's overall physical fitness and health.

docs.title: Reasoning (REA)
docs.text: Reasoning is a measure of a character's ability to learn, understand, and evaluate things.

docs.title: Spirit (SPR)
docs.text: Spirit is a measure of a character's spiritual strength.

docs.title: Determination (DET)
docs.text: Determination is a measure of a character's mental strength.

docs.title: Perception (PER)
docs.text: Perception is a measure of a character's ability to perceive their surroundings.

docs.title: Charisma (CHA)
docs.text: Charisma is a measure of a character's force of personality.

docs.title: Attribute Bonus
docs.text:

docs.title: Height
docs.text: How tall you are, in a measurement of your choosing.

docs.title: Weight
docs.text: How heavy you are, in a measurement of your choosing.

docs.title: Steel Drivin' Man
docs.text:
Automata do not have stamina points.

Any stamina points that the character would normally have should instead be added to their mana points. Any action that would consume stamina instead consumes mana. This grants the character a larger combined Mana and Stamina pool that can be used for either purpose.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Human is probably the most widespread of the world's many inhabitants. They make their homes wherever they feel and tend to pop up in the oddest of places for the strangest of reasons. It's not uncommon to see them at home deep in the cities of elves, the forests of dryads, or within the narcisse encampments. Like other species, their instinctual need for companionship leads them to seek out others of similar mindset and groups where they can easily integrate themselves; Unlike other species, they often have few if any qualms with who they make their companions, let alone their bed mates, which allows them to easily stray from their primary population centres.

Compared to others, the humans live relatively short lives and it shows. While individuals vary greatly in their temperament, the average human is volatile, impatient, and passionate to a fault. The truth of it is that humans are acutely aware of their limited time and tend to try to make the best of it and live without regrets. Desperate for purpose they latch onto people, places, ideals, even concepts. When something a human has come to hold dear is threatened, they react, in what is probably the biggest understatement of the century, extremely poorly. A human wronged has an unparalleled capacity for violence unadulterated by thoughts of restraint or reason. A human wronged will make you pay even if it's the legitimate last thing they do.

docs.title: Don't Fear the Reaper
docs.text: Whenever you are called upon to roll a resistance check, and the penalty for failure is death or unconsciousness, you may re-roll the check as if you had used one destiny point for a re-roll. You may do this at no cost regardless of the number of destiny points you have remaining.

docs.title: The Progression System
docs.text: In Reisender progression is the name of the game, figuratively speaking.
